setup.zh: 三百级石阶直通云雾，顶上站着一个扫地的老头：「不看出身，不看荐书——只看三样：腿，脑子，胆子。」一试，腿：三百级，一炷香。
setup.en: Three hundred steps climb into the clouds; at the top stands an old man with a broom: "Not birth, not letters — three things only: legs, wits, nerve." First trial, legs: three hundred steps, one stick of incense.

recap.zh: 一试，三百级石阶：你三步一吸，三步一呼，替舅舅走了上来。
recap.en: First trial, three hundred steps: three steps a breath in, three a breath out, you climbed the stair for your uncle.

zh: 石阶顶上，一个扫地的老头。
en: Three hundred steps, straight into the clouds.
At the top, an old man with a broom.
First trial, legs: one stick of incense.

story.zh:
九月初九。泗水，沉鼎山下，人山人海。

几千个孩子，挤在山门前。有穿绸子的，有穿布衣的，有光着脚的。马小宝站在最前面，身边跟着两个家丁，一个给他打伞，一个给他扇扇子。

今天没下雨，也没太阳。

山门前一道石阶，三百级，一直通进云雾里。石阶顶上，站着一个扫地的老头，拄着一把竹扫帚，看都不看底下这几千个孩子一眼。

**扫地的老头**：沉鼎观收人。不看出身，不看荐书——

马小宝的脸，白了一下。

**扫地的老头**：——只看三样。腿。脑子。胆子。

**一试 · 腿。**

三百级石阶。一炷香。

「开始」两个字还没落地，几千个孩子一窝蜂往上冲，冲得石阶上尘土飞扬，像一群被放出笼子的鸭子。
story.en:
The ninth day of the ninth month. The Si River, the foot of Chending Mountain — a sea of people.

Thousands of children, crammed in front of the mountain gate. Some in silk, some in cotton, some barefoot. Ma Xiaobao stands at the very front with two servants: one holding an umbrella over him, one fanning him.

It isn't raining today. There's no sun either.

Before the gate, a stone stair — three hundred steps — runs straight up into the clouds. At the top stands an old man with a bamboo broom, leaning on it, not so much as glancing at the thousands of children below.

**The old sweeper:** Chending Temple takes disciples. Not by birth. Not by letters of recommendation —

Ma Xiaobao's face goes white for a moment.

**The old sweeper:** — by three things only. Legs. Brains. Guts.

**First trial · Legs.**

Three hundred steps. One stick of incense.

The word "Begin" hasn't even hit the ground before thousands of children charge up in a swarm, kicking up dust all over the stairs, like a flock of ducks let out of the pen.

label.zh: 走在最后，三步一吸，三步一呼
label.en: At the back: three steps in, three steps out

exits.means: climbs steadily at an even pace, counting breaths, like a hunter on a long trail

story.zh:
你没有冲。你走在最后面。

你想起舅舅说的那句话：「我爬到一百六十级，腿就动不了了。」——虽然每年都在长。

你想起你爹说的：蹲一只鹿，蹲得越急，鹿越不来。

你一级一级地走，数着自己的呼吸。三步一吸，三步一呼。像在山里，追一头走得很稳的鹿。

冲在最前面的那些孩子，到了一百五十级左右，一个一个像腿上绑了石头，越急越走不动。有的坐在台阶上喘，有的干脆哭了起来。

马小宝在一百二十级就坐下了。两个家丁一左一右架着他，被扫地的老头远远看了一眼，又乖乖地把他放下了。

香快烧完的时候，山门底下忽然一阵吹吹打打。一顶滑竿，四个轿夫，抬着马小宝，一路小跑上了石阶。马小宝坐在滑竿上，手里还捏着一块桂花糕。

执事迎上去，接过一封盖着县衙大印的信，看了看，冲扫地的老头拱了拱手：「瞿老……荐书。按例，可补一试。」

扫地的老头没说话。他低下头，接着扫他那一级台阶，扫得很用力。

滑竿从他身边抬过去的时候，扫帚正好扫在一个轿夫的脚面上。轿夫一个趔趄，滑竿一歪——

马小宝是滚上第三百级的。

一百六十级。

你的腿也沉了，沉得像绑了两块磨盘。你没有停。也没有快。三步一吸，三步一呼。

{伴·阶}

香烧完的时候，你站在了第三百级石阶上。

你回头往下看了一眼。一百六十级那里，坐着好几个哭鼻子的孩子。

舅舅，你在心里说，我替你走上来了。

回去跟你说，就说我走了三百五十级。

扫地的老头，第一次抬起眼皮，看了你一眼。
story.en:
You don't charge. You walk at the very back.

You remember what your uncle said: "I got to the hundred-and-sixtieth step and my legs wouldn't move." — though the number grows a little every year.

You remember what your father said: wait on a deer, and the more impatient you are, the less it comes.

You climb one step at a time, counting your breaths. Three steps in, three steps out. Like following a deer through the mountains that walks very, very steadily.

The children who charged ahead get to about the hundred-and-fiftieth step and slow down one after another, as if stones were tied to their legs — the more they hurry, the less they can move. Some sit on the steps panting; some just burst into tears.

Ma Xiaobao sat down at step one hundred and twenty. His two servants hoist him up, one under each arm — the old sweeper glances at them from far away, and they set him down again, very obediently.

Just as the incense is nearly out, drums and horns strike up at the foot of the mountain. A litter chair, four bearers, and Ma Xiaobao in it, trotted up the steps, a sweet osmanthus cake still in his hand.

The steward meets them, takes a letter sealed with the county seal, reads it, and bows to the old sweeper: "Elder Qu… a letter of recommendation. By custom, it buys a second try."

The old sweeper says nothing. He bends to his one step and sweeps it, hard.

As the litter passes him, the broom catches a bearer's foot. The bearer stumbles, the litter tips —

Ma Xiaobao arrives at step three hundred rolling.

The hundred-and-sixtieth step.

Your legs are heavy now too, heavy as if two millstones were tied to them. You don't stop. You don't speed up. Three steps in, three steps out.

{伴·阶}

As the incense burns out, you are standing on the three-hundredth step.

You look back down once. At the hundred-and-sixtieth step sit several sniffling children.

Uncle, you say to yourself, I've climbed it for you.

When I get home I'll tell you it was three hundred and fifty.

For the first time, the old sweeper lifts his eyelids, and looks at you.

exits.means: rushes up the steps as fast as possible

story.zh:
你也冲了。几千只鸭子里，多你一只不多。

冲到一百五十级，你的腿忽然沉了——不是累，是像有人往你两条腿上，一边挂了一块磨盘。越急，磨盘越重。你身边的孩子一个接一个地坐下，有的喘，有的哭。

一百六十级。

你停下来，扶着膝盖，大口大口地喘气。这就是舅舅坐下的地方。二十年前，他在这儿坐了一炷香，看着别人一个一个从他身边走过去。

你想起你爹说的：蹲一只鹿，蹲得越急，鹿越不来。

你站直了。三步一吸，三步一呼。不快。也不停。

{伴·阶}

香只剩一指的时候，你站在了第三百级石阶上。腿抖得像两根面条。

扫地的老头抬起眼皮，看了你一眼。那一眼的意思大概是：鸭子里，也有会自己停下来的。
story.en:
You charge too. Among thousands of ducks, one more makes no difference.

At about the hundred-and-fiftieth step your legs suddenly turn heavy — not tired; it's as if someone had hung a millstone on each of them. The more you hurry, the heavier the millstones. The children around you sit down one after another, some panting, some crying.

The hundred-and-sixtieth step.

You stop, hands on your knees, gulping air. This is where your uncle sat down. Twenty years ago he sat here for a stick of incense and watched the others walk past him one by one.

You remember what your father said: wait on a deer, and the more impatient you are, the less it comes.

You straighten up. Three steps in, three steps out. Not fast. Not stopping.

{伴·阶}

With a finger's width of incense left, you are standing on the three-hundredth step. Your legs are shaking like two noodles.

The old sweeper lifts his eyelids and looks at you. The look says, more or less: even among ducks, there's one that knows how to stop by itself.
